report: The Internet of Things Connectivity Binge: What Are the Implications?
publisher: Pew Research Center and Elon University's Imagining the Internet Center

entries.label: People disconnect because of IoT attacks
entries.quote: As automobiles, medical devices, smart TVs, manufacturing equipment and other tools and infrastructure are networked, is it likely that attacks, hacks or ransomware concerns in the next decade will cause significant numbers of people to decide to disconnect, or will the trend toward greater connectivity of objects and people continue unabated?
entries.subject: internet of things security and disconnection
entries.note: Quote is the final sentence of a longer prompt about Internet of Things vulnerabilities.
entries.answer_mapping: agree = significant numbers will disconnect; disagree = most people will move more deeply into connected life

notes: One question from a canvassing of eight questions fielded 2016-07-01 to 2016-08-12. The question asks about 'the next decade' / 'the next 10 years' and names no year; target_year 2026 is read from that horizon (the jobs report itself says 'by 2026'). Non-random opt-in canvassing.
